what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A made-up studio and three made-up client sites, each one file and a vault app, show websites you own in practice.
sections.para: Kitewing Websites sells setup, a build from the client's material, design choice, QA and handover, with nothing monthly. Its three Harrowby clients, a potter's 28-piece catalogue, a community garden with events, rota and guides, and a plumber with a map and 19 guides, are single-file vault apps with data in JSON. The vaults are committed locally; pushing awaits the editor's token.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: A made-up studio, three different client sites, one file each, vault apps nested in a vault, previewed here.
sections.para: The studio sells the one-off model. Three sites in three industries each use a different design. Each is one HTML file with its data beside it, ready for an encrypted sgit vault, with the studio's vault holding the examples. They are served here as previews until the vaults are pushed.

sections.label: Kitewing Websites
sections.line: The studio site states the offer: five steps, one-off prices as hypotheses, ownership and no monthly fee.
sections.para: It explains setup, build, design choice, QA and handover, what clients pay and own, lift and shift, examples and FAQs: no page limit, undo through GitHub's history, hour blocks for help, and nothing to leave because everything is already the client's.

sections.label: Three made-up clients
sections.line: Three sites that sound complex but are easy for an agent: a catalogue, a community group and a trade's guides.
sections.para: Tidewrack Studio Pottery offers 28 filterable pieces with no checkout, staying static. Fennick Lane Community Garden has 15 events, a rota, news and 14 guides. Quillon Heat & Plumbing has services, a village map, emergency steps and 19 guides marked as sample guidance, gas work referred to registered engineers, and no invented reviews.

sections.label: How each one is made
sections.line: One HTML file each, data in content.json, no external requests, changeable by asking an agent, phone-checked.
sections.para: Styles, scripts and inline SVG are all in the page. Content loads from the vault, then fetch, then an inlined copy, so it works as a file. Owner requests like adding a mug or moving an event become edits to content.json. Each fits a 390-pixel screen.

sections.label: A vault in a vault
sections.line: Each site is an sgit vault that opens as the site; the studio's vault holds the three examples.
sections.para: The four vaults are created and committed locally; pushing needs the editor's access token. Until then the same files are served on the newsroom as previews, and public read keys will be published once pushed.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Everything is invented; the guides are sample text; the vaults are not pushed; prices are hypotheses.
sections.para: The studio, clients, town, people and prices are made up, the guides are not advice, and the previews are the same files that the vaults hold.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: A voice memo, the build brief, and related newsroom articles on owned websites and vault apps.
sections.para: The editor's memo of 26 October 2026 and the brief four agents built from, with articles on websites you own, the no-server studio, your own newsroom and the homepage as a vault.
